Human speech, identical audio

26 paired cases, built from 11 public human recordings across six languages. Five positive-word speakers have native-language declarations; Japanese is supplemental. Chinese declaration is for Chinese generally, with the file labeled Mandarin.

No synthesized voices. Audio decoded with FFmpeg 7.1 to mono 16 kHz, then silence-padded to three seconds. Corrections are splices of whole recordings, not natural self-corrections. Both providers receive identical bytes, the known language, and no expected-answer hint. Original source licenses apply to the audio; conversion, padding and any splicing are the modifications made here.

One speaker/take per target language; reused timing variants are not independent speakers. Native status is source/self-reported, not independently certified. This is a small sourced pilot, not a general accuracy estimate. Latency is measured after the entire clip is streamed, not from the end of the spoken word.
